exercises.en: The child hesitated before answering.
exercises.why: 머뭇거리다 means to hesitate; the other ~거리다 verbs describe shining, stickiness and sloshing.

exercises.en: Stars are twinkling in the sky.
exercises.why: 반짝거리다 describes something repeatedly shining or twinkling.

exercises.en: Jisu is looking for her own bag.
exercises.why: 자기 points back to the third-person subject, 지수.

exercises.en: The bus hasn't come yet.
exercises.why: 아직 with a negative means "not yet".

exercises.en: I don't drink coffee at all.
exercises.why: 전혀 with a negative means "not at all"; 별로 would only mean "not much".

exercises.en: The subway is much faster than the bus.
exercises.why: 훨씬 strengthens a ~보다 comparison; 별로 and 전혀 need a negative.

exercises.en: I bought a book about Korean food.
exercises.why: Before a noun (책) use 관한; 관해(서) goes before a verb.

exercises.en: I've gained a lot of weight lately.
exercises.why: 살이 찌다 is to gain weight; 찌 + 었어요 contracts to 쪘어요.

exercises.en: This coffee isn't very hot.
There are many restaurants around the station.
For now, I will wait here.
Minsu is still busy (as always).

reading.ko: 민수는 요즘 살이 많이 쪘어요. 작년보다 몸무게가 훨씬 많이 나가요. 민수는 일단 매일 공원에서 걷기 시작했어요. 공원 주위에는 나무가 많고 아주 조용해요. 살은 아직 별로 안 빠졌어요. 하지만 민수는 자기 자신을 믿어요. 요즘은 운동에 관한 책도 읽고 있어요.
reading.en: Minsu has gained a lot of weight lately. He weighs much more than last year. For now, he has started walking in the park every day. Around the park there are many trees and it is very quiet. He hasn't really lost weight yet. But Minsu believes in himself. These days he is also reading a book about exercise.

questions.q: 민수는 무엇에 관한 책을 읽고 있어요?

exercises.ko: 하늘이 어두워요. 오후에 비가 ___ 것 같아요.
exercises.en: The sky is dark. I think it will rain this afternoon.
exercises.why: For a guess about the future, use the ~(으)ㄹ modifier before 것 같다.

exercises.en: This movie will probably be fun (I haven't seen it yet).
exercises.why: A guess about something not yet experienced uses ~(으)ㄹ 것 같다.

exercises.en: It seems to be snowing outside right now.
exercises.why: A present action you judge from evidence takes ~는 것 같다.

exercises.en: It seems Minsu has already gone on vacation.
exercises.why: A past action takes the ~(으)ㄴ modifier before 것 같다.

exercises.en: This room seems really stuffy.
exercises.why: A present-tense adjective takes ~(으)ㄴ before 것 같다, never ~는.

exercises.ko: 저 식당이 비싸요? — 네, ___ 것 같아요.
exercises.en: Is that restaurant expensive? — Yes, it seems so.
exercises.why: 그렇다 becomes 그런 before 것 같다 ("it seems so").

exercises.en: You worked all day? You must be really tired.
exercises.why: ~겠어요 expresses a guess about someone else's state.

exercises.en: Wow, this shrimp must be really delicious!
exercises.why: ~겠어요 reacts to what you see with a guess: "it must be".

exercises.en: I think it will be peaceful there.
That person seems really stylish.
exercises.ko: 그 사람은 정말 멋있는 것 같아요.

exercises.en: It seems he already replied.
exercises.ko: 그 사람이 벌써 답장한 것 같아요.

exercises.en: That must be really amazing!

reading.ko: 다음 주부터 휴가예요. 저는 친구하고 바다에 갈 거예요. 거기는 아주 평화로울 것 같아요. 친구는 낚시를 좋아하고 저는 새우를 좋아해요. 하지만 다음 주에 비가 올 것 같아요. 그래도 괜찮을 것 같아요. 친구도 이 여행을 아주 기대하는 것 같아요.
reading.en: My vacation starts next week. I'm going to the sea with a friend. I think it will be very peaceful there. My friend likes fishing and I like shrimp. But it looks like it will rain next week. Still, I think it will be okay. My friend seems to be really looking forward to this trip too.

questions.q: 이 사람은 누구하고 바다에 갈 거예요?
다음 주 날씨는 어떨 것 같아요?

exercises.en: Minsu, you look like you're in a good mood today.
exercises.why: An adjective takes its ~아/어 form before 보이다.

exercises.en: This kimchi looks a bit salty.
exercises.why: 짜다 + ~아 보이다 contracts to 짜 보이다.

exercises.en: That child looked very happy.
exercises.why: 하다 adjectives become ~해 before 보이다; the tense goes on 보이다.

exercises.en: That cloud looks like a cat.
exercises.why: Noun + 같이 + 보이다 means "to look like" that noun.

exercises.en: I can see the fire station through the window.
exercises.why: 보이다 ("to be seen") takes the thing seen as its subject: 소방서가 보여요.

exercises.en: I can hear music from the next room.
exercises.why: With 소리가 as the subject, use 들리다 ("to be heard"), not 듣다.

exercises.en: I can't hear the music well.
exercises.why: The thing heard is the subject of 들리다, so it takes 이/가.

exercises.en: This drink tastes like strawberry.
exercises.why: Noun + 맛 같다 means "tastes like" that noun.

exercises.en: This studio apartment looks small.
That bag looks heavy.
That man looks like a student.
This smells like coffee.

reading.ko: 저는 오늘 새 원룸을 보러 갔어요. 원룸은 좀 작아 보였어요. 하지만 아주 깨끗해 보였어요. 창문으로 산이 보였어요. 밖에서 차 소리가 조금 들렸어요. 관리비는 조금 비싼 것 같아요. 하지만 저는 그 원룸이 마음에 들어요.
reading.en: Today I went to see a new studio apartment. The studio looked a little small. But it looked very clean. I could see a mountain through the window. I could hear a little car noise from outside. The maintenance fee seems a bit expensive. But I like that studio.

questions.a: 좀 작아 보였어요. 하지만 아주 깨끗해 보였어요.

exercises.ko: 배가 너무 ___ 라면을 두 개 먹었어요.
exercises.en: I was so hungry that I ate two packs of ramen.
exercises.why: 고프다 is ㅡ irregular, so it becomes 고파서.

exercises.ko: 어제 눈이 많이 ___ 학교에 안 갔어요.
exercises.en: It snowed a lot yesterday, so I didn't go to school.
exercises.why: Never put the past tense before ~아/어서; the final verb carries it.

exercises.en: My legs hurt, so I took a taxi.
exercises.why: 아프다 is ㅡ irregular: 아프 + 아서 becomes 아파서.

exercises.en: It's a long holiday, so Seoul Station is crowded.
exercises.why: 연휴 ends in a vowel, so it takes 라서.

exercises.en: Today is Sunday, so I'm not going to school.
exercises.why: 일요일 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이라서.

exercises.ko: 오늘은 일이 너무 많았어요. ___ 저녁을 못 먹었어요.
exercises.en: I had too much work today. So I couldn't eat dinner.
exercises.why: 그래서 starts a sentence that is the result of the one before.

exercises.en: It was hot, so I opened the window.
exercises.why: 덥다 is ㅂ irregular: 덥 + 어서 becomes 더워서.

exercises.en: I forgot my friend's name, so I felt really sorry.
exercises.why: 하다 verbs become ~해서, with no past tense before it.

exercises.en: The long holiday starts tomorrow, so I'm really excited.
I was busy, so I couldn't call.
It's not my bag, so I don't know.
I was sick yesterday. So I didn't go to school.
exercises.ko: 어제 아팠어요. 그래서 학교에 안 갔어요.

reading.ko: 지난 주말은 연휴라서 가족하고 부산에 갔어요. 고속도로가 너무 막혀서 다섯 시간이 걸렸어요. 저는 도시락을 깜빡했어요. 그래서 배가 많이 고팠어요. 부산에서 바다를 봤어요. 바다가 너무 예뻐서 기분이 좋았어요.
reading.en: Last weekend was a long holiday, so I went to Busan with my family. The highway was so jammed that it took five hours. I forgot my lunch box. So I was very hungry. In Busan I saw the sea. The sea was so pretty that I felt good.

exercises.en: I couldn't go to school because of the snow.
exercises.why: Noun + 때문에 means "because of" that noun.

exercises.ko: 내일 시험이 ___ 때문에 오늘은 공부할 거예요.
exercises.en: Because I have an exam tomorrow, I'll study today.
exercises.why: A verb or adjective needs ~기 before 때문에.

exercises.ko: 어젯밤에 잠을 못 ___ 때문에 너무 피곤해요.
exercises.en: I'm very tired because I couldn't sleep last night.
exercises.why: ~기 때문에 can carry its own past tense: 잤기 때문에.

exercises.ko: 제 동생은 학생___ 때문에 교복을 입어요.
exercises.en: My younger sibling wears a school uniform because they are a student.
exercises.why: With 이다, use 이기 때문에; 학생 ends in a consonant, so 이 can't drop.

exercises.en: The reason I was late is that the road was jammed.
exercises.why: End with ~았/었기 때문이에요 to give a past reason.

exercises.ko: 요즘 너무 바빠요. ___ 친구를 자주 못 만나요.
exercises.en: I'm very busy these days. Because of that, I can't see my friends often.
exercises.why: 그렇기 때문에 starts a sentence that follows from the previous one.

exercises.ko: 왜 안 먹어요? — 배가 안 ___ 때문이에요.
exercises.en: Why aren't you eating? — It's because I'm not hungry.
exercises.why: ~기 때문이에요 answers a 왜 question.

exercises.ko: 작년에 주식에 ___ 때문에 지금 돈이 없어요.
exercises.en: I have no money now because I invested in stocks last year.
exercises.why: The reason is in the past, so use ~았/었기 때문에.

exercises.en: I couldn't sleep because of the noise.
I don't want to do it because it's annoying.
The streets are crowded because it's the weekend.
It's because I dropped my phone.

reading.ko: 오늘 아침에 늦게 일어났어요. 어젯밤에 친구하고 오래 통화했기 때문이에요. 늦었기 때문에 세수도 못 했어요. 그리고 버스에서 휴대폰을 떨어뜨렸어요. 그렇기 때문에 지금 휴대폰이 안 돼요. 오늘은 정말 힘든 하루예요.
reading.en: I woke up late this morning. It's because I talked on the phone with a friend for a long time last night. Because I was late, I couldn't even wash my face. And I dropped my phone on the bus. Because of that, my phone doesn't work now. Today is a really hard day.

exercises.en: Grandmother is reading a book.
exercises.why: 읽다 ends in a consonant, so it takes ~으세요.

exercises.en: The teacher came from Korea yesterday.
exercises.why: ~시 goes before the past tense: 오 + 시 + 었어요 = 오셨어요.

exercises.en: My father lives in America now.
exercises.why: ㄹ stems drop the ㄹ before ~시: 살다 becomes 사세요.

exercises.en: Grandfather is sleeping in his room now.
exercises.why: 주무시다 is the honorific verb for 자다.

exercises.en: The teacher is in the classroom now.
exercises.why: For a respected person being in a place, use 계시다.

exercises.en: The teacher ate lunch.
exercises.why: 드시다 is the honorific verb for 먹다; 드리다 means to give.

exercises.en: I gave the teacher flowers.
exercises.why: ~께 is the honorific "to" used with 드리다.

exercises.en: I want to give Grandfather some coffee.
exercises.why: Giving to a respected person uses 드리다, not 주다.

exercises.en: My grandmother lives alone.
Is your mother at home?
The teacher answered my question.
I gave my grandmother a letter.

reading.ko: 그저께 할머니 집에 갔어요. 할머니는 부산에 사세요. 저는 할머니께 과일을 드렸어요. 할머니가 정말 좋아하셨어요. 저녁에 할머니가 맛있는 음식을 많이 만드셨어요. 할머니는 밤 아홉 시에 주무셨어요.
reading.en: The day before yesterday I went to my grandmother's house. My grandmother lives in Busan. I gave her some fruit. She really liked it. In the evening she made a lot of delicious food. She went to sleep at nine at night.

exercises.en: Please sit on the chair.
exercises.why: 앉다 ends in a consonant, so the polite command is 앉으세요.

exercises.en: Please go straight ahead. (very formal)
exercises.why: The most formal command is ~(으)십시오, spelled with 오.

exercises.en: Clean your room! (plain command to a child)
exercises.why: ~아/어라 is the blunt plain command; 하다 becomes 해라.

exercises.en: Don't be late. (casual)
exercises.why: ~지 말다 becomes ~지 마 as a casual command.

exercises.en: Please don't eat food here.
exercises.why: 말다 drops its ㄹ before ~세요: 마세요.

exercises.en: Get up quickly! (casual)
exercises.why: The casual command is the plain ~아/어 form; 일어나 + 아 contracts to 일어나.

exercises.en: Do not smoke inside.
exercises.why: Negative commands are verb stem + ~지 + a form of 말다.

exercises.en: Please go to the left.
exercises.why: 가다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ~세요.

exercises.en: Please don't worry.
Please come up here.
Wash your hands first. (to a child)
Please do not go in. (formal sign)

reading.ko: 엄마가 아이에게 편지를 썼어요. 일찍 일어나라. 일어나서 먼저 세수해라. 그리고 아침을 꼭 먹어라. 학교에서 친구하고 다투지 마라. 선생님 말씀을 잘 들어라. 늦지 마라!
reading.en: Mom wrote a letter to her child. Get up early. When you get up, wash your face first. And be sure to eat breakfast. Don't argue with your friends at school. Listen carefully to your teacher. Don't be late!

exercises.en: Please close the door.
exercises.why: 닫다 has ㅏ, so it takes ~아 before 주세요.

exercises.en: Please show me your ticket.
exercises.why: 보여 주다 means "to show"; 봐 주세요 would mean "please look at".

exercises.en: My father bought me a bicycle.
exercises.why: A respected person doing a favor for me: ~아/어 주시다; 드리다 is only for giving to them.

exercises.en: My friend helped me move.
exercises.why: 돕다 is ㅂ irregular and becomes 도와 before 주다.

exercises.en: Please don't touch my computer.
exercises.why: "Please don't" as a favor is ~지 말아 주세요.

exercises.en: Thank you for giving me a birthday present.
exercises.why: Thanking someone uses ~아/어서 + 고마워요, with no past tense before 서.

exercises.en: Thank you for waiting. (to a respected person)
exercises.why: With respected people, use ~아/어 주셔서 감사합니다.

exercises.en: Give me that pen. (casual)
exercises.why: The casual command of 주다 is 줘.

exercises.en: Please show me the menu.
Thanks for listening to me. (casual)
Please don't open my bag.
My colleague bought me coffee.

reading.ko: 어제 저는 왼발 발목을 다쳤어요. 그래서 걷기가 아주 힘들었어요. 동료가 제 가방을 들어 줬어요. 친구는 저녁을 만들어 줬어요. 저는 두 사람에게 정말 고마웠어요. 오늘은 동료에게 커피를 사 줄 거예요.
reading.en: Yesterday I hurt my left ankle. So walking was very hard. My colleague carried my bag for me. My friend made dinner for me. I was really grateful to both of them. Today I'm going to buy my colleague a coffee.

questions.q: 오늘 동료에게 무엇을 사 줄 거예요?

exercises.en: I listen to music when I exercise.
exercises.why: Verb stem + ~(으)ㄹ 때 means "when"; 하다 becomes 할.

exercises.en: I wear glasses when I read books.
exercises.why: 읽다 ends in a consonant, so it takes ~을 때.

exercises.en: When I was young, I lived in Busan.
exercises.why: For a time in the past, use ~았/었을 때: 어렸을 때.

exercises.ko: 제가 역에 ___ 때 친구가 기다리고 있었어요.
exercises.en: When I arrived at the station, my friend was waiting.
exercises.why: A completed past action takes ~았/었을 때.

exercises.en: What did you eat at lunchtime?
exercises.why: A noun takes 때 directly, with no ~을.

exercises.en: Every time I look at this photo, I smile.
exercises.why: 때마다 follows the ~(으)ㄹ form: 볼 때마다.

exercises.en: Please wait here until the bus comes.
exercises.why: 때까지 means "until".

exercises.ko: 저는 초등학교 때___ 한국 음악을 좋아했어요.
exercises.en: I have liked Korean music since elementary school.
exercises.why: 때부터 means "since" that time.

exercises.en: When I'm sad, I listen to music.
When I was in Korea, I ate a lot of kimchi.
exercises.ko: 한국에 있었을 때 김치를 많이 먹었어요.

exercises.en: I will go to Busan during vacation.
Every time I go to Seoul, I meet my friend.

reading.ko: 저는 어렸을 때 곤충을 아주 무서워했어요. 곤충을 볼 때마다 울었어요. 초등학교 때 선생님이 곤충에 관한 책을 주셨어요. 그때부터 곤충을 좋아하기 시작했어요. 지금은 시간이 있을 때 산에 가서 곤충을 봐요. 곤충은 정말 신기한 것 같아요.
reading.en: When I was young, I was very scared of insects. Every time I saw an insect, I cried. In elementary school, a teacher gave me a book about insects. From then on, I started to like insects. Now when I have time, I go to the mountains and look at insects. I think insects are really amazing.

questions.q: 지금은 시간이 있을 때 뭐 해요?
